description: Girard reduction replaces a zonotope by a simpler zonotope that still contains it. A *zonotope* is a center plus a list of generator vectors, and its *order* is the number of generators divided by the dimension `n`. The method sorts the generators by `‖g‖₁ − ‖g‖∞`, which is zero for a generator that points along an axis. It keeps the generators with the largest values and encloses all the others in one axis-aligned box, so at most `order · n` generators stay. The result is a *sound over-approximation*: it contains every point of the original set, and possibly more; the method is fast, and reachability tools run it after each step to keep the number of generators small.

papers.title: Reachability of Uncertain Linear Systems Using Zonotopes
papers.venue: Hybrid Systems: Computation and Control (HSCC), Lecture Notes in Computer Science

papers.title: Methods for order reduction of zonotopes
